title: Year 10 grammar and accuracy booklet
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 41 (Year 10 grammar and accuracy booklet (portal, sentence forms))
intro: Lesson 41: Language for effect: varied sentence forms and syntax. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Form
Example
Effect
rows: The corridor stretched ahead, lined with doors, each one closed, each one silent.
Who had left the light on?

model.title: Make it tense: 'I walked down the corridor and I heard a noise and I stopped and I turned around and there was nothing there.'

parts.text: Cut the 'and' chain into separate sentences
Use a long sentence to build the corridor
Use short sentences at the noise

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The corridor stretched ahead, lined with doors, each one closed. Then a sound. I stopped. Turned. Nothing.

keywords.def: the order and arrangement of words in a sentence
a phrase at the start that tells how, when or where
an incomplete sentence used for effect
how fast or slow writing feels to read

questions.q: Rewrite with varied openings: 'I opened the gate. I walked up the path. I knocked on the door.'
questions.a: For example: Pushing the gate open, I crept up the path. At the door, I hesitated. Then I knocked.

questions.q: Write a three-sentence moment that goes long, short, fragment.
questions.a: For example: The rain had been falling for hours, filling the gutters and drumming on every roof. It stopped. Silence.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a 150-word moment of tension (a power cut at home) using all four forms and three different openings. Starter: 'Without warning, ...'
questions.a: A tense paragraph with deliberate syntax: long build, short sentences and a fragment at the peak.

questions.q: Extend: mark each sentence form in the margin.
Stretch: explain one deliberate syntax choice in a sentence.
questions.a: For example: The fragment 'Nobody.' isolates the fear.

questions.q: Which version builds the most tension?
options: There was nothing there when I turned.
I turned. Nothing. Only the hum of the lights.
I turned around and there was nothing there except the lights which were humming.
questions.a: B) I turned. Nothing. Only the hum of the lights.. Short forms and a fragment slow the moment and create suspense.

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Short sentences speed the reader up and make each beat land like a heartbeat.
